title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia
talk_summary: Sally-Ann Delucia describes Arize's Alex agent and the context-management lessons from building it: naive truncation and LLM summarization failed, while head/tail truncation plus a retrievable memory store worked. She also advocates long-session evals and moving data-heavy work into sub-agents so the main conversation stays small.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep the start and end of long context, drop the middle from the prompt, and store the middle so the agent can retrieve it later.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we take the beginning still 100 characters. We also take 100 off of the tail.

takeaways.what_they_do: They tried LLM summarization but found it too inconsistent and lacking control over what mattered, so they moved to deterministic truncation plus memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it was too inconsistent. There was no control over what was important

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep the main conversation light and delegate data-intensive search/analysis to sub-agents, passing only results back.
takeaways.evidence_quote: offload the heavy tasks. The main conversation can stay small.

takeaways.what_they_do: They replay 10 turns and test the 11th to detect context degradation that only appears late in long conversations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we load 10 turns and then we test the 11th to understand how the context is doing.

takeaways.what_they_do: They store offloaded context in a database with IDs and give the agent a tool to fetch relevant earlier context by ID/preview.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have it saved off in a database with IDs
